questions.q: What was the actual root cause behind Finding 1 (Opportunity OWD being Public Read/Write)?
options: An old setup-wizard default that nobody revisited as the org grew
A deliberate decision to support a cross-selling program
A requirement from the compliance team
A restriction rule that was misconfigured
questions.explain: Interviews revealed nobody remembers choosing it deliberately — it was simply never revisited, exactly the pattern from Lesson 19's Mistake 1.

questions.q: What does Finding 2 (three near-identical profiles) recommend, and what pattern does it illustrate?
options: Deleting all three profiles with no replacement
Creating a fourth profile to merge the other three
Consolidating to one profile plus a permission set for the real differences — profile explosion
Converting the profiles into sharing rules
questions.explain: The three profiles differed by only two fields and one tab, so the fix consolidates to a single profile with a permission set carrying the Commercial Lines-specific access — exactly the profile-explosion pattern from Lesson 19.

questions.q: Why is the 'Data Migration Support' permission set flagged as a finding, even though it technically works as configured?
options: Because Modify All is never allowed in any permission set
Because permission sets cannot grant Modify All
Because it conflicts with the role hierarchy
Because it grants broad Modify All access to four users with no current migration and no documented reason for ongoing access
questions.explain: The concern isn't that Modify All is inherently wrong — it's an unexplained, seemingly stale broad grant left in place long after its original purpose, the access-accumulation pattern from Lesson 19.

questions.q: Why does Finding 4 (Claim_Investigation__c) rank first in the audit's priority order?
options: Because it's the easiest finding to fix
Because it represents active, ongoing exposure of sensitive in-progress investigation data
Because it was the first finding discovered chronologically
Because it requires the least user interviewing
questions.explain: The audit prioritizes by data sensitivity and current exposure, not ease of fix — and Finding 4 is live exposure of sensitive data, ranking it above the others.

questions.q: Why does the audit rank Finding 2 (profile explosion) as lowest priority despite being, per the lesson, the easiest fix?
options: Because it's a maintenance cost rather than an active data exposure
Because easy fixes are always deprioritized regardless of impact
Because profile consolidation is technically impossible
Because it doesn't appear in the compliance review scope
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly separates urgency from ease of fix: Finding 2 costs ongoing maintenance effort but isn't actively exposing data the way Findings 3 and 4 are.
